locator.text: Equation (8.10), p. 91, in the proof of Lemma 8.2

verdicts.summary: Lean has a weaker form of it. Same operator (the Fourier multiplier (2πi v_r·k)^{-1}, TorusInverse.multiplier) and the same shape of estimate, with the constant fixed before the source, but the derivative loss is larger and only p = 1 is stated as one declaration. inverse_finiteJets concludes a C^n bound on 𝓛^{-1}f from a C^{n+5} bound on f, where (8.10) at p = 1 asks for C^{m+4}: the extra order comes from the summable lattice majorant Σ_k weight(k)^{-4} (SmoothFourierData.summable_weight_inv_four, used through rapid_coefficient/coefficient_seminorm_bound with p+4 derivatives), against the paper's Σ_{k∈Z²}(1+|k|)^{-3}. No declaration was found for 𝓛^{-p} with the paper's single p+3 loss; higher p is reached by iterating one inverse at a time, which is why totalIntegral_finiteJets and exactAlias_finiteJets consume m + 6p input jets (5 per inverse plus 1 radial derivative per integration by parts) rather than the paper's ~2p+3. Two incidental differences in the Lean's favour: its inverse annihilates the zero Fourier mode by construction (multiplier d 0 = 0), so no zero-mean hypothesis on H is needed, and JetBound bounds joint parameter-and-torus jets, not only the paper's C^m_y (mixedJet_inverse_bound is the purely-y version, with the same loss 5).
